what: Skipping decode blocks that the sliding-window mask would zero anyway, in vLLM's Triton paged-decode kernel (vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py). Measured 2026-08-23/24 on gfx1100.
why: That kernel iterates every block of the sequence and then masks everything outside the window to -10000. On Muse-Glimmer-30B at 32768 context with a 2048 window that is 2048 blocks read where 128 are needed, and it accounted for 70.67% of decode CUDA time.
the_change: for j in range(0, num_blocks) becomes for j in range(first_block, num_blocks) with first_block = max(0, seq_len - SLIDING_WINDOW) // BLOCK_SIZE when SLIDING_WINDOW > 0. The mask keeps (context_len - seq_offset) < SLIDING_WINDOW with context_len = seq_len - 1, so the lowest surviving absolute index is seq_len - SLIDING_WINDOW and every block below it is masked in full. exp(-10000 - m) is zero, so this is an identity rather than an approximation. 11 lines including the comment. The block table stays full length: SlidingWindowManager.remove_skipped_blocks frees blocks that fall out of the window and writes the shared _null_block into their slots, so the skipped iterations were reading one block repeatedly rather than 32x the KV, and starting the loop later cannot index out of bounds. Read from single_type_kv_cache_manager.py rather than inferred from the outputs matching.
upstream_state: An equivalent change is already proposed upstream: vllm-project/vllm#49588, '[Kernel] Skip out-of-window KV blocks in paged decode sliding-window path', opened 2026-07-23 by @hec-ovi. Its executable lines are identical to these once the identifier and the argument order of tl.maximum are normalised; only the comment wording differs. It has been a draft since 2026-07-25 with no review comments. **Nothing here should be opened as a second PR**, and nothing has been. Its evidence and this evidence do not overlap: it reports a kernel microbenchmark on one gfx1151 board, 100 iterations of a single decode call with parameters shaped after poolside/Laguna-S-2.1 and correctness against a hand-written PyTorch reference at 0.002 tolerance, with no model run end to end and no upstream test suite. What is here is two real models end to end on gfx1100, three processes per cell across seven depths, upstream's own test file with no case changing outcome, and 15 boundary cases bit-identical. As of 2026-08-24 main still has the original loop.

machine.gpu: 2x Radeon RX 7900 XT (gfx1100), TP=2, VFIO guest
machine.note: the container also carries the PR#49991 clone flag (unset here) and PR#45916's split-KV with the gate widened; neither is on the path this measures

model_under_test.name: RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-INT4 (first of two; see models_affected)
model_under_test.params: 30B dense, compressed-tensors pack-quantized int4, group 128, symmetric
model_under_test.attention_backend: ROCM_ATTN, chosen by the platform's own priority order
model_under_test.port_note: vLLM support for this model merged upstream 2026-08-14, after this container was built. It runs here through a downstream adaptation: the three new files from the merge commit plus ~15 lines of registration, a load_weights rewritten to this version's stacked_params_mapping convention because WeightsMapper here has no orig_to_new_stacked, and one inlined is_vit_use_data_parallel fallback.

kernel_level.method: torch profiler, delay 2 active 8, 32768 context, rank 0; same settings as prof-mtp-31b.py

gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct.why: the largest sliding-window model here (window 1024, 50 of 60 layers) and the repository's workhorse
gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct.result: Unaffected, two runs per state. vLLM forces Gemma-4 onto TRITON_ATTN because its head dimensions are heterogeneous (head_dim 256 local, global_head_dim 512), and that backend's kernel already bounds its loop by the window. 8192: 24.27 before against 24.44 after; 32768: 33.10 against 33.16.

Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4.why: no sliding window, same ROCM_ATTN backend: the path the change must not disturb
Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4.result: Settled with three runs per state. 8192: 84.09 median before against 84.08 after; 32768: 95.42 against 96.69. The before and after ranges overlap at both depths, so the +2.6% seen in a single earlier run was process-to-process spread and not a regression.

reading: Two models reach this path and both gain, with the gain appearing exactly where the mechanism says it should. Below each model's window the change is worth 1.00x, and from there it grows monotonically with depth: gemma-3-27b 1.11x at 2048, 1.63x at 8192, 2.75x at 32768; Muse-Glimmer 1.15x at 4096, 2.01x at 16384, 3.15x at 32768. Three independent processes per cell with narrow ranges. Patched, Muse-Glimmer is nearly context-independent, 21.97 ms/tok at 512 against 26.63 at 32768. At the kernel it is 1.589 ms -> 154.796 us per call, 10.3x rather than the 16x the block count suggests, the difference being per-call overhead that does not shrink. Decode stops being attention-bound: attention falls from 74% of the step to 22%, and the 4-bit weight GEMM becomes the largest term. The gemma-3 figure is the one that shows the size of the problem: at 32768 it decodes at 8.06 tok/s unpatched against 30.36 for gemma-4-31B, a larger and newer model, purely because gemma-4 is routed to a backend that already bounds its loop.
scope: Any model with a sliding window that lands on ROCM_ATTN. That includes gemma-3, which is mainstream, and excludes gemma-4, which vLLM forces onto TRITON_ATTN because its head dimensions are heterogeneous. Checked and found not to qualify: Mistral-Small-3.2 and Mistral-7B-v0.3 (no window), Ministral-8B (window 32768, which covers the whole context at the depths measured), Phi-4-reasoning (no window), Phi-4-mini-reasoning (window 262144), GLM-5.2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Ornith-1.5 and LFM2.5 (no window, or a window with an architecture out of reach here). A small window relative to context is not common among 2026 flagships; Gemma is where it lives.
not_established: Two models on one machine, gfx1100 only. The 39 sliding layers still run at roughly 6.3 GiB/s of effective KV bandwidth after the change against 412 GiB/s for the custom HIP kernel in the same run, so their exclusion from that kernel is untouched; closing it would now be worth about 19%, not another 3x, because the weight GEMM dominates. **An earlier version of this file offered end-to-end token identity as the correctness argument. That test cannot discriminate on this machine and has been replaced by the two kernel-level results above; see gfx1100-greedy-nondeterminism.json.**

gemma-3-27b-it-quantized.w4a16.layers: 62, sliding_window_pattern 6 so roughly 5 local per global
gemma-3-27b-it-quantized.w4a16.why_it_matters: RedHatAI's w4a16 re-upload of google/gemma-3-27b-it, 344k downloads. head_dim is uniform and there is no global_head_dim, so the Gemma4-specific forcing rule in model_executor/models/config.py does not fire and it is not routed to TRITON_ATTN the way gemma-4 is. gqa_ratio 2 also puts the custom HIP kernel out of reach, so all 62 layers run on the Triton path.

verification.why: End-to-end token identity was the original correctness argument and it does not work on this machine; see nondeterminism below. These two are kernel-level with fixed inputs and are unaffected by it.

upstream_kernel_suite.what: tests/kernels/attention/test_prefix_prefill.py from the container's own source tree at /app/vllm, dated 2026-07-15 and matching the installed package. Run whole, unpatched then patched, compared per case from junit XML rather than by summary counts.

sliding_window_coverage.note: head sizes 24 and 128, num_queries_per_kv 1 and 64, both devices, kv_cache_dtype auto and fp8. The 224 skips are fp8_e5m2, which ROCm's custom paged attention does not support, and are identical in both runs.

upstream_kernel_suite.aside: The suite itself ran 2.6x faster patched, which is independent corroboration of the kernel change.

boundary_bit_comparison.what: 15 hand-built cases through the kernel directly, inputs constructed the way tests/kernels builds them, outputs saved and compared with torch.equal rather than allclose. Skipped blocks contribute exp(-10000 - m) = 0, so bit equality is the right bar.

coverage.window not a multiple of block_size: seq-unaligned-window, window 100 with block_size 16, first_block 118 of 126
coverage.no window at all: nowindow-bs16 and nowindow-bs32, bit-identical as required

boundary_bit_comparison.note: Both runs were separate processes and still agreed bit for bit, which places the engine-level nondeterminism below outside this kernel.
